checks.description: A unique H10-sized MMC below the exact H616 eMMC controller is admitted independent of mmc_host numbering using sysfs metadata only.
Absent, wrong-type/controller, undersized/oversized, malformed-capacity and ambiguous targets are rejected by tests.
The read-only diagnostic consumes the reusable helper without behavior regression; the helper opens no block node and no writer enters the production SD image.
Focused and existing SD/NFS tests, documentation checks and feature-workflow validation pass with physical identity and write limitations clearly stated.

constraints.text: For this measured test profile, require exactly 61,079,552 sectors. Do not carry forward the current 60–64 million-sector heuristic as write-target admission; a different module capacity requires an explicit reviewed profile value.

Fail closed when any additional MMC card or malformed/unreadable MMC candidate appears below the selected controller, even if one valid-capacity candidate exists. Test malformed numbers, trailing junk, overflow and ambiguous inventory; unrelated SD cards remain ignored.

Keep the helper limited to sysfs metadata and the existing read-only diagnostic. Preserve diagnostic output and behavior. The helper opens no block node; the existing diagnostic alone retains its bounded read-only environment open. Bind the helper source hash into the SD/NFS builder provenance manifest. Add no writer or write-target operation to the diagnostic composition, and do not treat the helper's returned path as sufficient identity for a later write.

Reconcile the proposal's statement excluding changes to the production SD image with its permission to compile the helper into the existing diagnostic: document that only the existing read-only NFS diagnostic and its build provenance may change, with no boot-chain or writer change.

Document that H10 has no CID evidence and offline fixture success does not prove installed-module identity, data preservation, rollback or physical write safety. H12 remains the separate hardware gate.

decision.rationale: H10 physically observed one MMC under the exact 4022000.mmc controller at 61,079,552 sectors. The separately verified QEMU writer targets only a synthetic USB disk. Before this improvement, the read-only locator is embedded in init.c, uses a 60–64 million-sector range, and tests only host numbering plus two in-range candidates. A small shared sysfs helper with exact measured-capacity and malformed/ambiguous-inventory refusal is a useful bounded improvement. The revised proposal permits compiling it into the existing read-only diagnostic; the builder currently hashes init.c as an input and must also hash the new helper source. The diagnostic executable is served by read-only NFS root, so the proposal's references to the production SD image must be interpreted as the existing SD/NFS diagnostic composition, not a new eMMC writer or write operation. H10 recorded no CID; controller, type and capacity cannot establish unique module identity or physical write safety. Decision 0018 and H12 retain the separate image, target, recovery, review and authorization gates. The helper adds negligible resource cost and no new runtime dependency.

evidence.limitations: Offline synthetic sysfs evidence only. No fresh SD image composition, physical eMMC identity, physical write, data preservation, rollback, or printer boot validation. H10 has no CID evidence; H12 remains required before whole-eMMC writes.
evidence.method: Reviewed the exact approved proposal and source diff; ran 10 focused SD/NFS and locator unit tests, static AArch64 diagnostic compilation with -Werror and _FORTIFY_SOURCE=2, py_compile, feature-workflow validation, local Markdown checks, and git diff --check. No image build or hardware access.
